reasoning_traces.think:
The Brain Injury Criteria (BIC) primitive defines a set of 18 scalar metrics derived from head kinematics to predict brain strain. These criteria act as a kernel in GSI’s Bayesian inference framework, enabling risk curve construction. The mapping from kinematics to criteria is deterministic but subject to subtype-specific failure modes. The Finite Element Strain Model provides an alternative, higher-fidelity mapping, serving as a benchmark for validation. The kinematic-to-strain mapping layer bridges these two systems, allowing GSI to extract interpretable features while maintaining fidelity to underlying physics. This system supports a triadic pipeline: impact retrieval → criteria scoring → strain estimation, ensuring consistency and reducing uncertainty through cross-validation.
